claim: For every integer \(k\ge1\), let \(\Sigma_k=\{a_1,\ldots,a_k\}\) and \(L_k=\{a_i a_i:1\le i\le k\}\). The minimum number of states of an epsilon-free NFA recognizing \(L_k\) whose underlying simple transition graph is a bipartite cactus is exactly \(k+1+\lceil k/2\rceil\), whereas the unrestricted epsilon-free NFA minimum is \(k+2\).

correctness.rationale: For each symbol, any accepting path has a distinct nonfinal middle state. In a cactus graph, a final state cannot serve three middle states because the resulting \(K_{2,3}\) subgraph makes edges belong to multiple four-cycles. Thus at least \(\lceil k/2\rceil\) finals are necessary; the explicit pair-block construction attains the bound and is bipartite. The unrestricted minimum \(k+2\) is separately witnessed and lower-bounded.

value.rationale: This is an exact parametric state-complexity invariant for a natural finite language family. It quantifies the precise overhead imposed by cactus topology: \(\lceil k/2\rceil\)-1 states beyond the unrestricted minimum, growing linearly for \(k\ge3\). The matching construction is reusable and the lower bound identifies the structural obstruction.
